📌 Toyosa adds BTC alongside USDT for Toyota purchases 

⚠️ Toyosa has introduced Bitcoin as a payment option for Toyota vehicle purchases in Bolivia, expanding its digital-asset checkout service one year after launching USDT payments. Eju TV reported that the company unveiled the Bitcoin service on Sept. 18 at Expocruz 2026 in Santa Cruz, where Toyosa said customers could now choose BTC alongside bolivianos, U.S. dollars and Tether’s USDT when purchasing a Toyota.

📣 BitGo confirmed the arrangement on Sept. 20, saying BitGo Bank & Trust supplied the institutional-grade digital asset wallet infrastructure behind Toyosa’s Bitcoin payment service. Its event calendar places the company at Expocruz from Sept. 18 through Sept. 21, providing separate confirmation of its presence in Santa Cruz during the launch. Toyosa’s Bitcoin service follows a crypto-payment system introduced at Expocruz one year earlier. In September 2025, Toyosa worked with BitGo, Towerbank and Tether to let customers purchase vehicles, parts and services using USDT.

🔔 Toyosa’s existing online payment page still describes the USDT workflow. Customers first obtain a quotation, select a supported blockchain network and scan a QR code from a crypto wallet. The page lists Ethereum and Tron among supported USDT networks and identifies Towerbank as the financial partner and BitGo as the blockchain technology provider. The public page reviewed on Sept. 20 had not yet been updated with a separate Bitcoin checkout guide, even though Toyosa and BitGo had announced that BTC purchases were available. Neither company had publicly disclosed supported Bitcoin wallet types, confirmation requirements, exchange-rate methodology or whether customers face transaction limits.

🖥 Iran moves closer to launching Shahid Soleimani satellite constellation: Minister

📌 Tehran, IRNA — Iran is preparing to take a major step toward developing satellite constellations, with three satellites set to be unveiled and launched as part of the country’s expanding space program, says the country’s minister of information and communications technology.

Sattar Hashemi has said three of the 24 satellites in the country’s Shahid Soleimani constellation are ready, which will be unveiled during the Islamic Revolution celebrations in February 2027 and placed into orbit before Norouz (March 20), marking a shift toward satellite constellations.
​
Hashemi said Iran must begin expanding communications coverage to remote villages, with settlements of more than 20 households included in plans. He acknowledged that connecting areas without terrestrial infrastructure may take time, but work must begin now.
​
Hashemi called for space policymaking to move from a supply-driven approach toward demand-driven development. He said technology is more valuable when users and societal needs are considered, adding that demand for space services should guide future development.
​
Satellite networks will not replace terrestrial infrastructure, fiber-optic networks, Hashemi said. Iran’s fiber rollout aims to strengthen fixed networks. He said satellite technology remains important for communications and remote sensing, including land management, water monitoring and mining.
​
Hashemi said advances in launch vehicles should also be viewed through an economic lens, as launch costs account for a major share of expenses. Deploying multiple satellites per launch and developing reusable launch vehicles can reduce costs, he said, praising contributors including martyred IRGC aerospace commander General Amir-Ali Hajizadeh.
​
Hashemi also stressed promoting space culture among younger generations. Children and teenagers should become familiar with space through programs and imagery, helping encourage them toward science and technology.
